data.long_meaning: Derived from Caroline, which is a feminine form of Charles. Charles means 'man, strong'. The name Karolina means 'pure, free woman'. In the Catholic Church, it is also given in honor of St. Carolus Borromeo. The name Karolina carries the meaning “Pure, Free Woman” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Karolina usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, free woman and live with faith, good character and purpose.

She married Archduke Ferdinand II of Tyrol and was the mother of Tyrolean ruler Ferdinand II, Holy Roman Emperor. In 1563, Carolina became the Abbess of the Cistercian convent in Seckau, Austria, and was known for her charitable works and contributions to the arts.

historical_references.context: Saint Karolina Kózák, also known as Karolina of Csábrág, was a Hungarian nun and mystic. She entered the Poor Clare Monastery in Nagyszalonta, Hungary, in 1742 and was known for her visions and ecstasies. In 1756, during the Austro-Turkish War, the monastery was attacked and destroyed, and Karolina and several other nuns were taken as prisoners to Istanbul. She lived in slavery for the next 13 years, enduring numerous hardships, but never gave up her faith. She was eventually released in 1769 and returned to Hungary, where she spent the remaining years of her life in prayer and contemplation. She was beatified in 1905 and canonized in 1991.
